## Historical documentation

For each event or primary-source artifact contributed to the class database, document the following information. Complete fields as precisely as possible. When information is uncertain or unavailable, use a brief note such as `Unknown`, `Approximate`, or `Not applicable` rather than leaving the field blank.

| Database field | What to enter |
|----|----|
| `record_id` | A unique identifier assigned to the entry |
| `event_or_artifact_name` | A concise, descriptive title |
| `record_type` | `Event` or `Artifact` |
| `date_start` | Start date or approximate year/date |
| `date_end` | End date, where applicable |
| `date_precision` | `Exact date`, `Year`, `Decade`, `Approximate`, or `Date range` |
| `location` | City, state/territory, region, nation, or another relevant location |
| `historical_period` | The broader historical period selected by your group |
| `summary` | A brief factual description |
| `major_event` | `1 = yes`; `0 = no` |
| `major_event_rationale` | Explain why the event does or does not meet your group’s criteria for a major historical event |
| `education_related` | `1 = yes`; `0 = no` |
| `education_connection` | Explain the item’s relevance to schools, teaching, learning, literacy, educational access, or policy; enter `N/A` when not applicable |
| `primary_source_title` | Title or description of the primary source |
| `primary_source_creator` | Person, organization, court, newspaper, institution, or other creator |
| `primary_source_date` | Date the primary source was created or published |
| `repository` | Archive, collection, library, or database where the source was found |
| `source_url` | Stable public URL or repository permalink |
| `citation` | Full citation in APA, MLA, or Chicago style |
| `trial_connection` | `Plessy`, `Brown`, `Both`, or `No direct connection` |
| `trial_connection_note` | Explain any connection to historical context, legal questions, educational access, or group research |
| `group_id` | Your timeline group identifier |
| `contributors` | Names of the students responsible for the entry |
| `verification_status` | `Draft`, `Reviewed by group`, or `Ready for class database` |

## Classification codebook

Use the following codes consistently so that the class can filter, sort, and visualize the shared database.

| Field | Code | Meaning |
|----|---:|----|
| `major_event` | 1 | The event meets the group’s stated criteria for historical significance |
| `major_event` | 0 | The event does not meet the group’s stated criteria for historical significance |
| `education_related` | 1 | The event or artifact directly relates to schools, teaching, learning, literacy, educational access, or education policy |
| `education_related` | 0 | The event or artifact does not directly relate to education |

## Documentation reminder

An entry can be historically significant without being directly related to education. Likewise, an artifact can be directly related to schooling or teaching without being classified as a major event.

For example, *Brown v. Board of Education* can be coded as both a major event (`1`) and education related (`1`). A local school-board record may be coded as not a major event (`0`) but education related (`1`).

Return to the [historical artifacts page](artifacts.qmd) for the full timeline activity, archive resources, group roles, and the connection between historical research and the Supreme Court trial reenactments.
